what: Bunge buys, ships, stores and processes agricultural commodities. It crushes oilseeds into vegetable oil and meal, refines edible oils, and after merging with Viterra it also has one of the largest grain origination networks in the world.
customers: Food manufacturers, animal feed producers, biofuel refiners and commodity buyers worldwide.
money: oilseed processing and grain origination and trading
edible oils for food manufacturers and consumers
moat: Port terminals, crushing plants and elevators placed along the routes crops travel from farm to ship, which lets it earn a margin on volume regardless of price direction.
risks: Net margin of about 1% is extremely thin
Crush margins have fallen as processing capacity expanded worldwide
Debt of about $18 billion after the Viterra merger
Biofuel policy changes swing demand for vegetable oil sharply
opportunities: Revenue grew about 32% last year as Viterra was consolidated
Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
The merger makes it a genuine global competitor to Cargill and ADM
watch: Crush margins and synergy delivery from the Viterra merger.
